newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat hopes to sign Hebron deal on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat hopes to sign Hebron deal on Tuesday.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said he hoped to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later on Tuesday to sign a deal on a long-awaited Israeli troop pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron.
Arafat spoke after meeting U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who arrived late on Monday to press the two sides for swift agreement on a Hebron withdrawal
Arafat, asked if he would meet Netanyahu later in the say to sign an accord, told reporters: "We hope so. If everything goes smoothly we can have this opportunity."

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have held marathon sessions to nail down final details of an agreement on a troop withdrawal from 80 percent of Hebron, the West Bank flashpoint from which the Jewish state was to have pulled back last March.
Netanyahu's predecessor, Shimon Peres, cancelled the planned pullout in response to Islamic suicide bombings that killed 59 people in the Jewish state in February and March.

After Netanyahu ousted Peres in an upset election victory in May, talks foundered over the hardline prime minister's demands for tightened security for the 400 Jewish settlers living in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
The negotiations were moribund until Clinton sent Ross to the region earlier this month.
Arafat said of the negotiators: "They are working through issues that are complex and in very great detail. They are working hard."
He declined to go into details, but said talks would continue on Tuesday morning.

A member of the Israeli negotiating team, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters he was also optimistic and that he was "anticipating a Netanyahu-Arafat meeting taking place on Tuesday to sign a deal."
